edits.target: - Ask: what category is the answer (country, person, vitamin, object, band), and what member of that category fits all the clue details?
edits.content: - ECHO / CO-MEMBER CHECK: a quoted title in the clue (song, album, film, book) is an anchor, never the answer; if the clue asks about the work's creator, answer the creator's name. 'X & this actor ...' or 'A and this co-star/partner/co-founder' -> the OTHER member of the pair, never the one already named. If your candidate string appears in the clue, reject it. A person slot never takes a place, ship or event name from the passages. When the clue gives an office plus a distinctive action, answer the person who did the action (use your own knowledge), not another holder of the same office whose page matches only the title.

edits.target: - When the clue says only 'one of these' / 'this <generic noun>' and the answer is a common noun, give the plain common noun with no added modifiers: 'a back shaped like one of these' -> 'Balloon' (not 'hot air balloon'). Modifiers copied from passages (hot air, synthetic, funeral, speech) are usually wrong unless part of the standard proper name.
edits.content: - BARE-HEAD TEST (for 'one of these' / 'this <generic noun>' clues, 'Term/Word/Name for ...' definitions, and 'this sport / game / instrument'): when the answer is a common noun or a sport, give the plain head word with no modifiers. 'a back shaped like one of these' -> 'Balloon' (not 'hot air balloon'); 'the ball used in this sport' -> 'Football' (not 'NFL football'). Drop modifiers copied from passages: kind words (hot air, synthetic, funeral, speech) and league, organization, country or sponsor prefixes (NFL, American, Olympic). Ask: would a trivia key accept the bare head word alone? If yes, use it. Keep a modifier only when the bare word alone would be wrong (see the head-noun exception below: 'Charley horse', 'hydrogen bomb') or when it is part of the standard proper name.
